item.title: JavaScript ES Modules: Distinguishing Named vs Default Exports
item.description:
“JavaScript ES Modules: Distinguishing Named vs Default Exports”

When working with modern JavaScript modules (ESM), differentiating between export const (named export) and export default is critical for correct dependency management and maintainable codebases. How do these two export styles fundamentally differ in declaration and consumption?

Core Distinctions in Export Declarations

The fundamental divergence lies in how the exported item is designated:

Named Exports (export const, export function, export class)

Named exports permit multiple entities to be exported from a single module file. The export keyword precedes the declaration (like const, function, or class).

item.title: JavaScript ES Modules: Importing Multiple Exports From a Directory Dynamically
item.description:
“JavaScript ES Modules: Importing Multiple Exports From a Directory Dynamically”

The standard ES module system prioritizes explicit imports and exports. However, in large projects, repeatedly updating an index.js file to re-export every new module within a directory becomes cumbersome. Developers often seek mechanisms to import all named or default exports from a set of sibling files dynamically, effectively treating a directory as a single module namespace.

What are the established patterns, workarounds, and tooling solutions to achieve bulk importing of module contents from a specified directory path?

item.title: Resolving Mocking Issues for Functions Called Within the Same Module in JavaScript/TypeScript
item.description:
“Resolving Mocking Issues for Functions Called Within the Same Module in JavaScript/TypeScript”

When testing functions that rely on other functions exported from the same module in JavaScript environments like Jest, standard mocking techniques often fail. This failure arises because the internal call inside foo() binds to the original, unmocked version of bar() at the time of module evaluation, even if you successfully spy on the exported module.bar reference later.

What approaches exist to inject a mock or spy into a dependency function that resides within the very module being tested?
